text:
Mira: Quick heads-up — I ran the week-long trace against the new continuous-batcher heuristics. Observed a weird half-life on prefill queue size where KV priming seems to decay faster than expected.
Alex: Can you paste the top-line numbers?
Mira: Sure. From the 10M request sample: prefill_queue_half_life ~ 1.8s (target ~4s), kv_cache.hit_rate dropped 0.63 -> 0.42 after we separated the init/gen lanes.
Samir: Oof. That explains the decode spikes I saw on the 3080 pods last night. Lower hit rate => more kv cold loads => kernel fallbacks.
Pat: Do we think it's the token_budget_target or the batch formation window?
Mira: Short thread: batching window went from adaptive 12-60ms to 8-40ms to reduce latency tail. That inadvertently shortened effective KV priming time for prefill cohorts.
Alex: So prefill vs decode separation reduced shared batching that used to keep KV warm. We trade tail latency for more cold KV wakes.
Samir: I dumped a microprofile. Kernel switches increased 2.1x on generation heavy flows; context switch logs show more frequent kernel_fallback paths. Snippet: 
```
kernel_choice: fast_attn_v1 -> fallback_matmul at tok=24
kv_cache.load_time_p50: 4.2ms -> 12.8ms
```
Mira: Proposed tweak: reintroduce a tiny overlap window (prefill tail join = 25ms) and bias batch formation to prefer requests with non-empty KV in the 1st slot. Keeps warm paths without reintroducing big latency.
Pat: Can we do an experiment config? Something like: 
```
"batch_window_ms": {"min":8, "max":40, "prefill_tail_join_ms":25},
"token_budget_target": {"prefill":12, "decode":8},
"kv_priming_pref": "prefer_warm_first_slot"
```
Samir: I'll run a synthetic with duplicated prefixes to stress KV and measure kernel change rate.
perf-bot: Benchmark job #4432 finished — p50 latency down 2% overall, p99 decode up 9%, kv_cache.hit_rate overall -0.18. Full report: https://ci/redwood/perf/4432
Alex: Okay next steps: Samir runs the KV-biased batcher test, Mira runs a live canary with prefill_tail_join=25ms for 2h on a slice of traffic, Pat validates token_budget targets don't blow throughput. Report back by EOD. :thumbsup:
Mira: Added the canary config to staging. Will post short logs when it runs.
Pat: If this keeps kernel fallback high we should consider a fast path kernel that tolerates slightly colder KV rather than fallback to matmul. CC @Samir for kernel implications.
Samir: Noted. If canary shows >1.5x kernel fallback we pause.
